answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow, like an onyx vault, before it may earn: the stake is returned only after peers attest honest work over several epochs. A single fake identity is cheap, but a pearl of reputation must be built slowly — faking a thousand agents means locking a thousand stakes and doing a thousand epochs of real work. Marble-cold economics: the attacker pays upfront and only recoups by behaving, so mass fakery costs more than it can ever earn back.
